solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tree on top of mountain is unshakeable

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on top of another means it comes first in the answer

parts.note: a fir is a conifer
M is a map abbreviation for mountain

explanation.surface: A tree perched on a mountain summit stands firm against the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something firm is steady and resolute, a straightforward synonym for not able to be shaken.

clue.text: Follower often of status with odd requirement for meeting

parts.note: the phrase status quo: this Latin word often follows status
rum is British slang for strange or odd

explanation.surface: Someone status-conscious who tags along has a peculiar demand before attending a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum meaning odd is old-fashioned British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A quorum is the minimum number of members who must be present for a meeting to conduct business.

clue.text: Catalogue biological grouping if unknown

parts.note: class is a taxonomic rank between phylum and order
taken as written
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: A scientist hesitates to catalogue a biological group whose identity is not yet known.
explanation.definitionFit: To catalogue things is to sort them into categories, which is what classifying means; both are verbs.

clue.text: Family installing large oven

indicators.note: to install something is to put it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: kin are relatives
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A household has a big new oven fitted in their kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln is a type of furnace or oven used for firing pottery or drying materials.

clue.text: Exhausted area with duke interring king

indicators.note: to inter is to bury, so one letter is buried inside the rest

parts.note: a zone is an area
D is the abbreviation for duke
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A worn-out region where a duke has buried a king.
explanation.walkthrough: The king goes in after the first three letters of the area word.
explanation.definitionFit: Zonked is informal slang for utterly tired or worn out, matching the adjective.

clue.text: Personnel weapon exploded in mortar's casing

indicators.note: in places the scrambled letters inside the other piece
something blown apart has its parts scattered, so the letters are rearranged
a casing is the outer shell, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the outer letters of mortar, first of the pair
letters to be scrambled
the outer letters of mortar, last of the pair

explanation.surface: Military staff are hurt when a weapon goes off inside the shell of a mortar.
explanation.walkthrough: Casing means just the outside letters of mortar, which wrap around the scrambled weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Manpower is the workforce available, the people employed, which is what personnel means.

clue.text: Concerned with seeing us reflected in glass bottle

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a vial is a small glass container for liquids

indicators.note: a mirror reflection shows things back to front

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: Seeing our own reflection in a glass bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Visual is the adjective relating to sight, so it describes anything to do with seeing.

clue.text: I cry a river, which indicates constant pressure

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the noun it describes: a line which indicates constant pressure

parts.note: taken as written
to sob is to cry
taken as written
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone complains about weeping a river of tears under constant strain.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase cry a river suggests heavy emotion; here each word is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map an isobar is a line joining points of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Confine naughty child reportedly out of bed

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so a sound is wanted, not a spelling

parts.note: having got up, someone has risen

explanation.surface: A parent sends a misbehaving kid back to their room for getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprison someone is to lock them up, keeping them restricted, a synonym for confining them.

clue.text: Retained most of key part

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, before its tail goes
PT is the standard abbreviation for part

explanation.surface: Someone held on to most of an important section.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept is the past tense of keep, and keeping something means holding on to it, a synonym of retained.

clue.text: Beginning of summer affected island's seafood

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter
camp means theatrical or affected in manner
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Early summer has had an effect on an island's catch of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: Scampi in Britain are breaded langoustines, a pub-menu staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are Norway lobsters or large prawns, a kind of shellfish eaten as seafood.

clue.text: I con gal excitedly to embrace Joker, using flattery to get results

indicators.note: embracing someone means wrapping arms around them, so the jumble surrounds another letter
acting excitedly means moving about wildly, so the letters get jumbled

parts.note: letters to be scrambled
J marks the joker in a pack of cards; Joker is also this setter's name

explanation.surface: A con man brags about tricking a woman, with the setter himself pulled in, by sweet talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter, Joker, slips his own initial into the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cajoling means coaxing or wheedling someone with flattery to get them to do what you want.

clue.text: Pay for what bow and arrow do

definitions.meaning: first meaning: provide funds for, as with a bequest
second meaning, read cryptically: both of these words finish with the same two letters, so the clue describes how they end

explanation.walkthrough: Bow and arrow suggest archery, but the second definition is about spelling: each word ends -OW, giving END OW.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give money to fund something permanently, such as a college chair, so it means pay for.

clue.text: Swap farthings and threepenny bits?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: trade one thing for another
second meaning: coins that are no longer in use, former small money

explanation.walkthrough: Farthings and threepenny bits were old British coins withdrawn before and at decimalisation, so they are former change; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An exchange is the act of giving one thing and receiving another, the noun sense of a swap.

clue.text: Specify five — just half ten

indicators.note: only half means keeping two of the four letters and dropping the rest

parts.note: taken as written, before it is halved
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Someone asked to name five is told that is only half of ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just half ten' tempts one to read five as half of ten; in fact half applies to five, and ten stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix a date or price is to settle on it and state it definitely, a synonym of specify.

clue.text: Jack in the morning: my, that's lucky!

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
a.m. means before noon
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at Jack's good fortune one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: Jammy is British slang for lucky, usually said with mild envy.
explanation.definitionFit: Jammy is informal British for fortunate, especially undeservedly so, the same sense as lucky.

clue.text: Quieten beast of burden, very loud inside

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: a mule is a pack animal
fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Silencing a pack animal that is braying very loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To muffle a sound is to deaden or soften it, making it quieter, so it is a synonym of quieten.

clue.text: Joker, perhaps, holds old whiskey and chicken

indicators.note: something that holds things contains them, so other letters go inside

parts.note: a joker is an example of a playing card; perhaps signals the example
O is the abbreviation for old
whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The setter Joker is holding an old whiskey and some chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: Joker is also the setter's name, so it looks like the setter is the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is slang for a person lacking courage, a coward.

clue.text: Grow pale when accepting it

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so another piece goes within

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone blanches at the moment they have to face up to the situation.
explanation.definitionFit: To whiten is to become white or lose colour, so as an intransitive verb it means to blanch.

clue.text: Staff's first sign of split with tons leaving

indicators.note: something that leaves departs, so those letters are removed

parts.note: cleft means split, as in a cleft chin
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: Staff note the first hint of a rift in the organisation as heavyweights depart.
explanation.walkthrough: Staff here is the musical stave, not employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is the symbol at the start of a musical stave fixing the pitch of its lines.

clue.text: Woodwind instrument recital arranged around noon

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters surround another letter
arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: letters to be scrambled
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A woodwind instrument recital is scheduled for around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet is a single-reed member of the woodwind family.

clue.text: Fish, grouse or beef
A little variable as to direction

indicators.note: a little of the following words means only a small run of their letters is used

parts.note: runs from the end of variable across as and into to

explanation.surface: Something is somewhat uncertain about which way to go.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four compass points, an example of a direction.

clue.text: Strong resentment about lake fisherman

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: anger is strong displeasure
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A fisherman is bitter about the state of the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler is someone who fishes with a rod and line.

clue.text: Lubricant's good — runs with lack of effort

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
ease is freedom from difficulty

explanation.surface: A good lubricant makes machinery run effortlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease is a thick oily substance applied to moving parts to reduce friction, a kind of lubricant.
